text:
rajesh: Quick sync: prototype idea for a "decision-tree" fallback service that composes multiple policies (SLO, error-spike, confidence-drift) into ranked actions. want input on shape and failure modes.
emily: sounds promising. can you outline why tree vs score? pros/cons?
rajesh: brief: tree lets us short-circuit (fast path) for obvious cases and attach different cooldowns per branch. score is simpler for tuning but harder to express ordered mitigations.
pat: ops concern: branching multiplies state we must store per-tenant. we need tiny state (action+expiry) or sticky tokens only.
lena: for canaries we already keep session cookies for sticky routing, so storing a small record per session is ok. but prefer TTL-based entries in redis with eviction.
rajesh: agreed. design: runtime asks /decide once per request when no sticky token present. service returns [action, version_hint, ttl, metadata]. runtime caches per-session if sticky.
emily: what are example actions? I propose: NOOP, SLOW_PATH(block heavy ops), SWITCH_VARIANT(vX), SPLIT(traffic %) , MIRROR, RETURN_STUB.
pat: add RATE_LIMIT(client_rate) as an action for bursty degradation.
lena: question: how does tree pick split %? do we couple with rollout controller percentages or decide adaptively?
rajesh: both. rollout controller seeds target split; decision-tree can override temporarily based on short-term risk score (e.g., drop canary to 0% if p99>500ms AND error>2%). That override decays back toward rollout target.
emily: important: use "confidence bands" for metrics so we avoid noisy flips. compute banded deltas over 3 windows (1m, 5m, 30m). tree nodes reference bands, not raw numbers.
pat: telemetry placement: runtime emits light envelopes (p95,p99,err,latency_histogram_signpost,model_confidence_hint). heavy aggregation done off-path in the metrics pipeline. decide service subscribes to aggregated windows for each tenant. also allow request-provided quick signals for very fast local checks.
lena: sticky token semantics: if SWITCH_VARIANT returned with sticky=true, runtime must honor until sticky ttl, independent of action ttl. this prevents "yo-yo" effect.
rajesh: fail modes: if decide service unreachable -> runtime falls back to local conservative heuristics: honor rollout controller target, but route to MIRROR + RATE_LIMIT 50% as a safe default.
emily: security note: do not send full inputs to decide service. only context (tenant, model, route, small sample signals). redact any PII.
pat: logging/audit: every automated action must emit an audit record with top-3 rule triggers. tag with rollout id and request sample id when available.
lena: canary lifecycle integration: rollout controller should surface an API to attach policy bundles (tree definitions) to a rollout id. decide service stores policy per rollout id and evaluates with variant metadata.
emily: testing: add a harness that replays historical metric windows and validates action trajectory. plus a synthetic-fault job that simulates slowdowns and checks cooldown/hysteresis.
rajesh: implementation sketch:
- policy authoring: small DSL (yaml) with nodes, predicates (band ops), actions, transition weights.
- runtime RPC: POST /v1/decide (tenant, rollout_id?, session_id?, context, quick_signals) -> {action, ttl, sticky, reason[]}
- storage: redis for sticky mapping + postgres for audit + kafka events for offline analysis

pat: would like sample DSL snippet in RFC. show node that says "if p99_band > baseline*1.4 and error_rate_band > 2% then return SWITCH_VARIANT:quantized-v2 with ttl 120s"
emily: ops: provide a debug UI that shows per-tenant active decisions and reason tree. RBAC restrict. also allow manual override to pin fallback for troubleshooting.
lena: perf: decision path must be <2ms median. cache common answers (per-route+tenant) and avoid blocking hot request paths.
rajesh: rollout: start with canary-only scope (10 tenants) and forced mirror for first week. measure false positives and tune bands.
pat: ownership and runbook: ops to own canary-gateway; eng infra to own SDK runtime changes; eng-sre to own alerting thresholds. I'll add to runbook.
ops_bot: note recorded: created ticket INFRA-2897 for redis sizing & RBAC gates.
canary-bot: reminder: prototype branch pushed -> canary-decision-tree:pr-78. run e2e nightly.
emily: thanks team. I'll write the RFC + sample DSL and assign reviewers. :rocket:
